newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish analysts play down Zalm's remarks on EMU.
newsitem.headline: Spanish analysts play down Zalm's remarks on EMU.

text.p: Spanish financial analysts on Tuesday played down Dutch Finance Minister Gerrit Zalm's remarks on Monday that it would be wiser for many states to take time meeting single European currency goals.
"It didn't have so much impact in the markets because the issue (is) not something that can be approved at these levels," said Carmen Hernansanz, economist at Merrill Lynch in Madrid.
Zalm is a politician rather than a central banker, and some analuysts said it was unusual for politicians to make the type of pronouncement Zalm made.

"The only unusual thing here is where the declaration came from," Bank of America economist Juan Antonio Mielgo said. "This is the first time a politician has made a statement against some countries entering the EMU from its start."

Zalm, who will chair meetings of European Union (EU) finance ministers for the next six months, said many countries would be better off waiting to join the European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) to ensure their deficit targets were sustainable.
Earlier on Tuesday, Portugal reiterated its "unflinching" determination to join the EMU at its launch in 1999.
But Spain, which had repeatedly made a similar assertion in the recent past, remained silent. A spokesman at the economy ministry said "there was no reaction on the issue."

The bond market shrugged off the remarks, closing almost unchanged from Friday's level. The March long-term future was up two points at 1610 GMT at 112.04, after opening weaker. Spanish markets were closed on Monday for a holiday.

The 10-year spread over German Bunds, usually considered a good indicator of how the market prices the European convergence process, was trading around 98 basis points, close to its all-time record low.

Economists said the only factor driving the Spanish bond market at present was the economic growth in the United States and the possibility that the Federal Reserve could decide to pick up the interest rates.
"At present, the only factors in the market are the conomic indicators in the United States," Mielgo said.
